v_cruise.help: Forward speed with a clear road (lane following).

v_avoid.help: Forward speed while steering around a duckie (far end of the proximity ramp).

v_min.help: Creep floor, above the ~0.05 friction stall limit with a small margin. Used when close to a duckie or in unknown geometry.

k_steer.help: Proportional steering gain. omega = k_steer * (0.5 - target_x) * 2, which equals k_steer * lane_error in lane following - i.e. this IS the lane P-gain. Matches the proven Challenge-1 value; raise if the bot understeers and crosses lines, lower if it oscillates.

omega_rotate.help: In-place rotation rate in ESCAPE_ROTATE. Must be high enough to break static friction when v=0 - too low and the bot buzzes but does not turn.

omega_max.help: Hard cap on |omega| for any command. 4 = the 'very abrupt' end of the usable range.

lane_margin.help: Hard inset from each detected line. The steerable corridor is [left_wall+margin, right_wall-margin].

duckie_margin_base.help: Lateral inflation added to each side of a far duckie's box.

duckie_margin_gain.help: Extra lateral inflation added proportional to proximity (ymax). A close duckie is inflated by base + gain.

gap_min_width.help: Minimum normalized width of a free interval to count as passable. Below this, the controller rotates to escape.

front_slice_half.help: Half-width of the central 'is something in my path' probe, around the column the bot is actually steering toward. Represents the ROBOT'S OWN WIDTH in normalized image x, not a comfort zone. HARD CONSTRAINT: keep it below gap_min_width/2 (currently 0.05). If it is wider, the two duckies forming the edges of an accepted gap fall inside the probe while the bot drives between them, front_block fires on the gap's own walls, and the manoeuvre is abandoned a frame or two after it starts. Was hardcoded at 0.18 against a gap_min_width of 0.1, which made every accepted gap self-aborting. The node warns at startup if this constraint is violated.

react_ymax.help: Closeness (ymax, bottom-of-frame = closer) a duckie must reach before it counts at all - creates its blocked interval and can trigger avoidance. HIGHER = react closer/later, LOWER = react farther/earlier. This is the knob for 'reacts too early'. Keep it below front_slow_ymax.

front_slow_ymax.help: Nearest front-duckie ymax where forward speed starts ramping down toward v_min. Keep above react_ymax.

front_block_ymax.help: Nearest front-duckie ymax where the front is considered blocked (no forward path) -> ESCAPE_ROTATE.

escape_min_dwell.help: Minimum time to stay in ESCAPE_ROTATE before it may exit (anti-chatter). NOTE: escape_min_dwell * omega_rotate is the minimum angle swept before the bot can reconsider - at 0.25 * 1.5 that is ~21 deg. Push it much higher and the lane lines leave the camera frame before the state can be re-evaluated, which is how the bot ends up driving blind.

avoid_min_dwell.help: Seconds AVOID is held once it starts on a passable gap, even if the gap momentarily measures narrower than gap_min_width. This is the 'drive through it confidently' knob. Duckie inflation grows with proximity (duckie_margin_base + duckie_margin_gain * ymax), so a gap accepted at range ALWAYS narrows as the bot approaches it - without a dwell the manoeuvre aborts partway through by construction. A duckie genuinely close ahead (front_block_ymax) still aborts immediately, so raising this does not disable the safety stop. Raise if the bot still gives up mid-gap; lower if it commits to gaps it should have rejected.

lane_hold_frames.help: Consecutive invalid lane-border readings before that side's line is treated as absent and the corridor opens on that side. This is line MEMORY: while the streak is below this, the last known line position is still enforced as a hard wall. Too low and a brief loss of sight (e.g. mid-rotation) releases the constraint and the bot drives over the marking; too high and it keeps steering away from a line that is genuinely gone.

duckie_hold_time.help: Seconds a duckie's span is kept after detections stop arriving (blind pass). Raising it stops a spin from erasing the duckie that caused the escape; but the span is stored in IMAGE x, so a stale duckie sits at the wrong bearing once the bot has turned or driven past it. Above ~1.5 expect phantom obstacles. A proper fix needs heading-indexed memory.

escape_relax_after.help: After rotating this long with no passable gap, progressively relax gap_min_width and inflation until a gap opens (anti-permanent-freeze).
